newsitem.title: CHINA: China hospital says Deng corneas to give light.
newsitem.headline: China hospital says Deng corneas to give light.

text.p: The last physical relic of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping that will not vanish with his death -- his corneas -- have gone to China's premier eye hospital, medical officials said on Monday.
"Our whole hospital is very moved by this," said one nurse at the Tongren hospital in central Beijing, China's most prestigious eye hospital and keeper of the capital's only eye bank.
"Deng's corneas are here," she said on Monday, speaking as the rest of the patriarch's body was being cremated at the Babaoshan cemetery in western Beijing.
"We hope they will provide hope and light for our future," she said. It was not known whether the corneas of Deng, who died last Wednesday aged 92, would in fact be used.

"Comrade Xiaoping's corneas should be donated to an eye bank and his body be dissected for the purpose of medical research," his family wrote in a letter just before his death, in line with his own wishes for his funeral.
Deng's ashes are to be scattered at sea.

The man whose capitalist-style reforms and open-door policy transformed an isolated Stalinist state into a fledgling world superpower had always abhorred the near-hysterical cult of personality that surrounded his predecessor Mao Zedong.
He had requested a simple funeral.
His decision to donate his corneas to an eye bank has inspired 440 people in the central city of Nanjing to follow his example, Shanghai's Wen Hui Bao newspaper said on Monday.
The volunteers, aged from 20 to 88, had offered to donate their body parts to medical research, the newspaper said.
Chinese people traditionally prefer to be buried whole, a preference that has led to difficulty in securing body parts for life-saving operations such as kidney transplants.
